turns.en: I think AI may exceed the sum of human intelligence in about five years.
turns.zh: 我认为 AI 可能在五年左右超过人类智能的总和。

turns.en: In five years?
turns.zh: 五年？

turns.en: Roughly five years is my guess. So there really won't be anything that AI can't do better than humans apart from being human perhaps.
turns.zh: 大约五年是我的猜测。所以真的没有什么 AI 不能比人类做得更好的，也许除了做人本身。

turns.en: In a more prosaic level, what will life be like?
turns.zh: 更实际地说，生活会是什么样子？

turns.en: The most likely outcome is an age of amazing abundance where anyone can have anything they can think of. This may sound preposterous but well here we are in 2026. Let's see where we stand in 2036. Now of course there are things that could derail this like a massive global thermonuclear war or something like that. But assuming that there's not World War III, I think we're headed for an age of amazing abundance. So, this is, I guess, a message of optimism and excitement about the future.
turns.zh: 最可能的结果是一个惊人的富足时代，任何人都可以拥有他们能想到的任何东西。这听起来可能很荒谬，但我们现在是 2026 年。让我们看看 2036 年时我们处于什么位置。当然，有些事情可能会破坏这个，比如大规模的全球热核战争之类的。但假设没有第三次世界大战，我认为我们正走向一个惊人的富足时代。所以，我想这是一个关于未来的乐观和兴奋的信息。

turns.en: You're sure that humans will no longer be in control in 10 years time?
turns.zh: 你确定人类在 10 年后将不再掌控局面？

turns.en: I think it is unlikely. In the same way that if the difference in intelligence between AI and humans is vastly greater than the difference in intelligence between AI and chimpanzees, it's hard to imagine that the chimpanzees would be in charge.
turns.zh: 我认为这不太可能。就像如果 AI 和人类之间的智能差异远大于 AI 和黑猩猩之间的智能差异，很难想象黑猩猩会掌权。

turns.en: I'm really sorry. We are essentially an evolved form of chimpanzee. So it wasn't that long ago that we were swinging through the trees eating bananas in the jungle and we still eat bananas.
turns.zh: 我真的很抱歉。我们本质上是一种进化了的黑猩猩。所以就在不久前，我们还在丛林里荡来荡去吃香蕉，而且我们现在还吃香蕉。

turns.en: You said there was a 10 to 20% chance of killer robots wiping out humanity. So you sounded worried then. Now you seem very relaxed about it. Have you changed your view?
turns.zh: 你之前说过有 10% 到 20% 的概率出现杀人机器人毁灭人类。那时你听起来很担心。现在你似乎对此很放松。你改变看法了吗？

turns.en: I still think there's risk associated with AI and robots. It's not zero. I guess I've come to my philosophical conclusion is to look on the bright side. I can't see any way to really stop this incredible momentum of AI and robots. And at times I sort of think, well, perhaps, even if there was a stop button, we probably shouldn't press it, because the most likely outcome is incredible abundance for all.
turns.zh: 我仍然认为 AI 和机器人存在风险。它不是零。我想我已经得出了我的哲学结论，那就是往好的方面看。我看不到任何真正阻止 AI 和机器人这股惊人势头的方法。有时我会想，嗯，也许，即使有一个停止按钮，我们也不应该按下去，因为最可能的结果是惊人的富足。

turns.en: That's what I thought actually. It struck me that now you seem to have decided it's inevitable. Let's hope for the best and go for the ride.
turns.zh: 这实际上也是我的想法。我突然意识到，你现在似乎已经断定这是不可避免的了。让我们怀着最好的希望，享受这段旅程吧。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, yes, pretty much. Let's enjoy the ride is my philosophy at this point because I mean honestly there seems to be just an inexorable progress here in AI and in robots. But even if I wanted to stop it, I don't think I could.
turns.zh: 是的。我的意思是，基本上是这样。享受旅程是我此刻的人生哲学，因为老实说，AI 和机器人方面似乎有着不可阻挡的进步。但即使我想阻止它，我也认为我做不到。

turns.en: Do you think there's still a 10 to 20% chance that killer robots mean the end of humanity? That's a high p(doom) as they say.
turns.zh: 你认为仍然有 10% 到 20% 的概率杀人机器人意味着人类的终结？这就是他们所说的高毁灭概率。

turns.en: Well, in the long run, we're all dead of course. According to the standard model of physics, the end of the universe is a long boring sort of thin gray soup of gradual cooling – the heat death of the universe. So if the heat death of the universe is the outcome for our reality, then it really is all about the journey because the destination is terrible.
turns.zh: 嗯，长远来看，我们当然都会死去。根据物理学的标准模型，宇宙的终结是一种漫长乏味的、逐渐冷却的稀薄灰色汤——宇宙的热寂。所以，如果宇宙热寂是我们现实的结局，那么关键真的在于过程，因为结局太糟糕了。

turns.en: But 10 years is not very... Yeah, I get that. But that could be a long way and you're basically very long way.
turns.zh: 但 10 年并不是很……是的，我明白。但那可能是一段漫长的路，而且你基本上走了很远。

turns.en: If it's 10 to 20% in 10 years, would you go into one of your rockets if you thought there was a 10 to 20% chance of it blowing up and killing you?
turns.zh: 如果 10 年内有 10% 到 20% 的概率，你会进入你的火箭之一，如果你认为有 10% 到 20% 的概率它会爆炸并杀死你？

turns.en: Yes. But let's say there's you can't do anything about it. Mhm.
turns.zh: 是的。但可以说你对此无能为力。嗯。

turns.en: I guess the only thing we can try to do is minimize the probability of the bad outcome. But trying to stop the intelligence in robots... I mean for the longest time I declined to participate in AI, or created OpenAI as essentially a counterweight to Google because at the time they had more or less a monopoly on AI. And then having Anthropic spin out of that, and now currently Anthropic is leader in AI. But these actions have actually resulted in knock-on effects that accelerated AI, which wasn't really my intention. So it just seems like all roads lead to acceleration of AI. So I'm like, okay, well, you can just sort of be sad about it or join the club, I suppose.
turns.zh: 我想我们唯一能尝试做的就是最小化坏结果的概率。但试图阻止机器人的智能……我的意思是，很长一段时间我拒绝参与 AI，或者创建 OpenAI 作为对 Google 的制衡，因为当时他们或多或少垄断了 AI。然后让 Anthropic 从中分拆出来，而现在 Anthropic 是 AI 的领导者。但这些行动实际上产生了连锁反应，加速了 AI，这并非我的本意。所以似乎所有道路都通向 AI 的加速。所以我想，好吧，你可以为此感到悲伤，或者加入俱乐部，我猜。

ts.sec: Past actions and acceleration of AI

turns.en: Well, you've certainly joined the club.
turns.zh: 嗯，你肯定已经加入俱乐部了。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: You definitely joined the club. If you can't beat him, join them, you know.
turns.zh: 你确实加入了俱乐部。打不过就加入，你知道的。

turns.en: A number of the other leaders of model makers have been pushing for different ways to try and minimize the risks. Just last week, Demises came out with a proposal for a private public regulator. Do you think you guys should be working more actively to get something in place to control the risks or do you think that's impossible too?
turns.zh: 其他一些模型制造商的领导者一直在推动不同的方法来试图最小化风险。就在上周，德米斯提出了一项关于公私监管机构的提案。你认为你们应该更积极地推动建立某种机制来控制风险，还是你也认为这不可能？

turns.en: Yeah, my recommendation to Dennis – because I talked to him for a few hours before he published his piece – was that the most immediate thing we could do is to have the leading AI companies at least just meet or have some sort of call once every few weeks and just discuss any safety and security issues.
turns.zh: 是的，我给丹尼斯的建议——因为在他发表文章之前我和他谈了几个小时——是我们能做的最直接的事情是让领先的 AI 公司至少每几周见个面或打个电话，讨论一下安全与安保问题。

turns.en: But why haven't you done that yet? I mean you don't all like each other very much. Yeah. But you're not all – I mean you're also all competing, right? You all want to be first.
turns.zh: 但你们为什么还没这么做？我的意思是你们并不都喜欢彼此。是的。但你们并不都是——我的意思是你们也在竞争，对吧？你们都想要成为第一。

turns.en: Yes. But that's where I think the competitors can keep each other honest. So meaning, if someone in the government who doesn't have a deep technical understanding and isn't driving the frontier of AI, it's quite difficult for them to know whether something should be released or not. However, the competitors, if given a week or two to review a new model, can highlight issues and have an incentive to keep all the competitors honest.
turns.zh: 是的。但正是在这一点上，我认为竞争对手可以互相监督。意思是，如果政府中的人没有深厚的技术理解并且不处于 AI 前沿，他们很难知道某个东西是否应该发布。然而，竞争对手，如果给一两周的时间审查一个新模型，可以指出问题，并且有动机让所有竞争对手保持诚信。

turns.en: So you'd have a system where the model makers would check each other's work. If there was something that worried them, you'd tell the government. Yeah. The government would then think, okay –
turns.zh: 那么你们会建立一个系统，让模型制造商互相检查对方的工作。如果有让他们担心的事情，你们会告诉政府。是的。然后政府会想，好吧——

turns.en: If there's something that was worrisome and that company was not doing anything to address that risk, then that would be the moment for government to step in and take action.
turns.zh: 如果有令人担忧的事情，并且那家公司没有采取任何措施来解决那个风险，那么那就是政府介入并采取行动的时机。

turns.en: Does all this have to happen?
turns.zh: 这一切都必须发生吗？

turns.en: Well, I think it would be good to do that immediately, really.
turns.zh: 嗯，我认为最好立即这样做，真的。

turns.en: Yeah, that's what people keep telling me. We have to get some kind of system in the next 6 months because of the pace at which the models are improving.
turns.zh: 是的，人们一直这样告诉我。我们必须在接下来的 6 个月内建立某种系统，因为模型改进的速度。

turns.en: Yeah, 6 months is a long time.
turns.zh: 是的，6 个月是很长的时间。

turns.en: So you think shorter than that?
turns.zh: 所以你认为比这更短？

turns.en: Well, I mean there are so many AI breakthrough announcements, sometimes multiple per day. I mean, how many were there last week?
turns.zh: 嗯，我的意思是 AI 突破性的公告太多了，有时一天好几个。我是说，上周就有多少？

turns.en: A lot.
turns.zh: 很多。

turns.en: I lost track, you know.
turns.zh: 我都记不清了，你知道。

turns.en: Yeah, a lot.
turns.zh: 是的，很多。

turns.en: So you basically, whether it's Demis' proposal or others, you need to get together and get this set up kind of now. It sounds like you're telling me.
turns.zh: 所以，你的意思是，无论是戴米斯的提议还是其他的，你们需要现在就聚在一起把它建立起来。听起来你是在告诉我这个。

turns.en: Yeah. I would recommend that we at least have some sort of informal call, weekly or bi-weekly, and that there's maybe a week or two weeks of early access by competitors. This is why I think the incentives work: because competing companies are likely to understand if something is a security risk and they won't be shy about highlighting that their competitor's models should be delayed in release.
turns.zh: 是的。我建议我们至少安排某种非正式的电话会议，每周或每两周一次，并且让竞争对手提前一周或两周访问。我认为这样激励机制是有效的，因为竞争公司很可能理解什么是安全风险，他们不会不好意思指出竞争对手的模型应该推迟发布。

turns.en: You guys don't much like each other and you don't much trust each other. You're insulting each other on social media constantly. So, do you think you can do that with people that you dislike, where there seems to be such personal vitriol between some of these leaders?
turns.zh: 你们彼此不太喜欢，也不怎么信任。你们经常在社交媒体上互相辱骂。那么，你认为你能和那些你不喜欢的人这样做吗？其中一些领导者之间似乎有如此个人化的恶意。

turns.en: Yes. Well, I'm not a fan of Sam Altman because if you started a nonprofit that was meant to be an open-source AI company and owned by the world, and it somehow got turned into an $800 billion for-profit company with closed source, I think you'd be like, 'Well wait a second, that's the exact opposite of what I donated the money for.' That's my issue. I think it's a legitimate one. And then Dario, I think, also is not a fan of Sam Altman. In fact, the reason the Anthropic team left OpenAI is because they didn't trust Sam Altman; otherwise Anthropic wouldn't exist. They would still be at OpenAI. I think Dario is a very principled person. He cares about things a lot, cares about the future of the world. And everyone I've met at Anthropic so far, no one set off my evil detector. They always seem well-intentioned. The road to hell is mostly paved with bad intentions. There are a few well-intentioned paving stones in there, so we don't want to be complacent. But at the end of the day, if we have to talk, we'll talk. I mean, set aside our personal differences for the good of the world type of thing.
turns.zh: 是的。嗯，我不喜欢山姆·奥特曼，因为如果你创办了一个本应是开源人工智能公司、归全世界所有的非营利组织，而它却变成了一个闭源的 8000 亿美元营利性公司，我想你会说：‘等等，这和我捐款的初衷完全相反。’这是我的问题。我认为这是一个合理的问题。而且，我认为达里奥也不喜欢山姆·奥特曼。事实上，Anthropic 团队离开 OpenAI 的原因就是他们不信任山姆·奥特曼；否则 Anthropic 根本不会存在，他们还会留在 OpenAI。我认为达里奥是一个非常有原则的人。他非常关心事物，关心世界的未来。到目前为止，我在 Anthropic 遇到的每一个人都没有触发我的邪恶探测器。他们看起来总是出于善意。通往地狱的道路多半是由恶意铺成的。其中也有一些善意的铺路石，所以我们不能自满。但归根结底，如果我们必须对话，我们会对话。我的意思是，为了世界的利益而把个人分歧放在一边那种事。

consensus.en: AI may surpass total human intelligence in about 5 years.
consensus.zh: AI可能在约5年内超越人类总智能。

consensus.en: The most likely outcome is an age of amazing abundance.
consensus.zh: 最可能的结果是一个令人惊叹的富足时代。

consensus.en: Humans will likely no longer be in control within 10 years.
consensus.zh: 人类很可能在10年内不再掌控局面。

consensus.en: There is a 10-20% chance of catastrophic AI outcome.
consensus.zh: 存在10-20%的灾难性AI结果概率。

consensus.en: Trying to stop AI is futile; we should enjoy the ride.
consensus.zh: 试图阻止AI是徒劳的，我们应该享受这个过程。

consensus.en: Competitors should review each other's models for safety.
consensus.zh: 竞争对手应该互相审查模型的安全性。

contrarian.en: AI surpassing humans is not bad; it leads to abundance.
contrarian.zh: AI超越人类不是坏事，会带来富足。

contrarian.en: The heat death of the universe means the journey matters more.
contrarian.zh: 宇宙热寂意味着旅程比终点更重要。

contrarian.en: Open-sourcing AI was a mistake; closed-source is safer.
contrarian.zh: 开源AI是个错误，闭源更安全。

contrarian.en: Competitors keep each other honest better than government.
contrarian.zh: 竞争对手比政府更能互相制衡诚实。

contrarian.en: Personal dislike can be set aside for safety discussions.
contrarian.zh: 个人厌恶可以为了安全讨论而搁置。

contrarian.en: Even if a stop button existed, we probably shouldn't press it.
contrarian.zh: 即使有停止按钮，我们可能也不该按下。
